author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize reports verified Reflection Beam 1.0 scores: ARC-AGI-2 23.5% at $0.61/task and ARC-AGI-1 74.0% at $0.31/task. Best scores use xhigh reasoning; high reaches 20.0% on ARC-AGI-2 at about 43% lower cost.
whyItMatters: New official model evaluation. Linked result page independently read in Chrome: semi-private best scores match. This is benchmark evaluation, not a Kaggle team score.

author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize places Argon behind Astra’s 99.9% ARC-AGI-3 result. It reports 62% fewer actions than the human baseline on the 25 public games, matching or beating three speedrun records and coming within 10% on six others.
whyItMatters: Keep the public-demo action comparison separate from the semi-private Verified score.

author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize says API issues prevented complete standard-harness testing: low reasoning completed 42/55 games for 49.8%; medium completed 46/55 for 46.3%; high completed 19/55 and no score was published. Reported scores retain partial credit across all 55 games. Provider adapter preserves opaque reasoning and permits automatic compaction; standard harness carries notes between turns. Costs use introductory $2 input/$10 output per million tokens.
whyItMatters: Material limit on harness comparisons. Do not present incomplete standard-harness runs as a clean capability ceiling.

author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize announces Gemini 4 Argon Verified results: ARC-AGI-3 97.5% at $4.8K with the provider adapter and 49.8% at $5.8K with the standard harness; ARC-AGI-2 91.3% at $0.32/task and ARC-AGI-1 98.5% at $0.16/task. It calls Google DeepMind the second frontier lab above 95% on ARC-AGI-3.
whyItMatters: Consequential organizer result. Separate from Kaggle standings. Standard-harness API incompletion is essential context; primary results introduction says 91.2% on v2 while its table and announcement say 91.3%.

author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize’s October 13 announcement reports DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at about 3% with its provider adapter and below 1% with the standard harness. The original linked verified-results table, refreshed October 14, gives a matched Low-reasoning comparison of 3.26% versus 0.35%; its headline best configurations differ in reasoning level. Organizer model evaluation, separate from Kaggle team submissions.
whyItMatters: Public original read without sign-in in the in-app browser; linked primary results table independently read. Organizer evaluation, separate from Kaggle team standings.

author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize announces Tufa Labs reclaimed first on the ARC-AGI-3 public Kaggle board with roughly 69%, up from roughly 56%. This is the author’s dated October 13 observation; refresh standings before publication.
whyItMatters: Organizer confirmation of a consequential team result already covered in the newspaper’s morning/afternoon reporting; no methods disclosed.

author: 82deutschmark
summary: Mark Barney publicly welcomes Jack Cole to his ARC-AGI-2 team, using a Professor X metaphor, and states an ambition to reach gold. The post has ARC Mutants artwork. The announcement explicitly concerns ARC2; it does not add Cole to ARC3 Team Turducken.
whyItMatters: Fresh public first-person confirmation supporting the commissioned ARC Mutants dispatch. Gold is an ambition, not an awarded medal.

author: spisallyouneed
summary: Sam Pasupalak announces SKY-001, which he calls the first Engineering World Model. He claims higher IoU on CAD and BIM tasks than tested frontier models, with 51–125 times faster and 150–210 times cheaper operation. Says it reflects 18 months of work by a team from Maluuba. Observed in Chollet’s repost inventory.
whyItMatters: Adjacent research lead amplified by an organizer; author claims only, with no independently inspected evaluation or ARC score. Repost action time is unknown.

author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize says Beam costs use Baseten pricing of $1.30 input and $4.30 output per million tokens. ARC-AGI-3 results are pending.
whyItMatters: Keeps the cost basis and absence of ARC-AGI-3 results explicit.

author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize links its leaderboard, public reproduction repository, testing policy and full Beam 1.0 results.
whyItMatters: Primary follow-up with reproducibility and policy links; group with the Beam announcement.

author: mhmazur
summary: Mazur launched ChatGPT Then and Now, pairing 492 early LearnGPT responses with new GPT-6 Astra answers. The linked page identifies the originals as December 2022–March 2023, new runs as October 19, 2026, one message with no system prompt and default reasoning effort, and says Claude Opus 5.5 wrote the paired analyses. A data download is offered; it was not downloaded.
whyItMatters: Public organizer product/research lead; a prompt comparison collection, with no ARC score or competition result claimed.

author: tufalabs
summary: Tufa says its two NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks are live in Stockholm; credits DELTA for installation and T.Loop for hosting and links a deployment video. Actual public post read.
whyItMatters: Contender infrastructure announcement; no evidence here ties this equipment to a specific score or competition run.

author: JFPuget
summary: Puget says AI agents now run all his training experiments, while he still reads their harness code. He says agents tend to overengineer, retain unnecessary compatibility code and require human direction. Actual public post expanded and read.
whyItMatters: First-person account of a competitor’s research workflow; no new ARC score claimed.

author: AlexBarry4
summary: Replying to Psyho’s PuzzleScript benchmark announcement, Barry says Epoch might be able to support API costs and that he has sent a DM. This is a tentative public statement; no funding agreement or collaboration is established.
whyItMatters: New response to the archive’s independent benchmark lead; recheck any later public confirmation before describing support as secured.

author: GregKamradt
summary: Kamradt publicly replies that he sent a DM to Psyho after Psyho announced a nearly finished private PuzzleScript-based reasoning benchmark.
whyItMatters: Organizer interest in an independent game benchmark; the message contents and any collaboration are unknown.

author: FakePsyho
summary: Asked about online solutions and prior model knowledge, Psyho says the selected games are niche and that reviewing logs for all selected games revealed no suspicious behavior.
whyItMatters: Author-reported contamination check; does not independently establish absence of training exposure.

author: FakePsyho
summary: Psyho reports full-run costs of $700 for Sol 6.1 and $60 for Luna 6, and estimates about $1,000 for Sonnet 5.5 and $4,000 for Astra 6. Says testing uses xhigh and may reduce generous action limits to lower cost.
whyItMatters: Separates reported completed costs from forecasts; no logs, scores or reproducible release verified.

author: FakePsyho
summary: Psyho says a nearly finished PuzzleScript benchmark selects 40 games from over 300, uses Codex/Claude Code harnesses with code generation prohibited, and keeps the game set private. The author says generous action limits already allow some saturation while models remain inefficient.
whyItMatters: Potential benchmark-development story; author claims, not an official ARC release or independently verified score.

author: iiiiitsu_ne
summary: Replying after NT congratulates them on passing 70, Itsu says they do not yet know how to improve beyond 70 and will keep trying.
whyItMatters: Attributed contender reaction, with thread context; no method or new official result established.

author: iiiiitsu_ne
summary: Itsu says they strongly expect to fall from rank eight on the private leaderboard, and perhaps on the public board too. This is their expectation, not a private result. The post links ARC-AGI-2.
whyItMatters: New first-person reaction from a top-ten contender; distinguish the rank mentioned at posting from later board observations.
